name: Fredericia
title: Fredericia Ship Thickness Measurement | Tanker & Bulk UTM
description: Thickness measurement in Fredericia for crude and product tankers, bulk carriers and feeders: ballast tanks, deck, cargo lines and pre-docking gauging.
h1: Ultrasonic Gauging of Tankers, Bulk Carriers and Feeders at Fredericia on the Little Belt
intro: Fredericia stands at the northern end of the Little Belt, where the crude oil pipeline from the Danish North Sea reaches the coast and a refinery shares the waterfront with container, bulk and breakbulk quays. That mix brings crude and product tankers, dry bulk carriers, general cargo ships and container feeders to the port, often for loading stays long enough to open a few tanks. When a superintendent wants readings from one of these ships, Atlantis sends a technician team from India to join her at the berth.

highlights.h: Crude loading at the pipeline terminal
highlights.p: Tankers lifting North Sea crude from the export facilities beside the refinery lie at the jetty for the whole of loading. Segregated ballast tanks pumped out as cargo comes aboard, the forepeak, void spaces and the main deck are the realistic gauging targets.

highlights.h: Product tankers on short regional trades
highlights.p: Refined fuels leave Fredericia on smaller tankers trading around the Baltic and North Sea. Many are older ships making repeated short voyages, where deck plating, cargo pipelines on deck and the segregated ballast tanks need watching between dockings.

highlights.h: Readings that set up a Funen docking
highlights.p: Ships needing a dry dock after a Fredericia call often go on to the repair yard at Lindø on Odense Fjord. Ballast tank and deck readings taken alongside here let the yard plan steel renewal before the ship arrives.

port.h: Fredericia: an energy port at the mouth of the Little Belt
p: Fredericia was founded as a fortress town on a point of land where the Little Belt narrows between Jutland and Funen, and its harbour still faces that strait. Ships reach it from the Kattegat through the northern approaches to the belt, without passing under the two bridges that cross the water further south-west towards Middelfart. The Little Belt is a narrow channel and the current in it can run hard, so pilotage, berthing and departure are planned around the stream and the weather, and an inspection team that wants to board at a fixed hour needs that plan from the agent. The harbour is deep enough to take sizeable tankers and bulk carriers, which sets it apart from many of the smaller harbours on the east coast of Jutland and explains why heavy energy and bulk trades settled here.

Energy shapes the traffic. Crude oil from the Danish North Sea fields arrives by pipeline across Jutland and is stored and exported from facilities beside the Crossbridge Energy refinery, so crude tankers load at the port, while product tankers carry refined fuels out to Danish and Baltic markets. A container terminal handles feeder services connecting Jutland with the large North Sea hubs, and the port company has invested in that business in recent years. Dry bulk carriers load and discharge at the bulk quays, and the breakbulk berths see project and general cargo for industry in the Triangle region around Fredericia, Vejle and Kolding. Coasters and small general cargo ships trading to the Danish islands fill the gaps between the larger callers, so the harbour sees ships of very different ages and sizes in the same week.

Port stays are long enough to be useful but rarely generous. A crude tanker's loading time sets the window, and her cargo tanks stay closed and inerted throughout; what opens up is the segregated ballast, emptied as the ship deepens, together with the forepeak, voids and the deck. Bulk carriers working cargo with grabs give hold access as each hatch is finished. Feeders on fixed rotations offer the narrowest windows, often only a few hours. Winter brings no regular ice to the Little Belt, but autumn and winter gales can keep ships alongside longer than planned or waiting outside, and those delays are sometimes the best chance a superintendent gets to add readings to a call. Fredericia also sits at the junction of Denmark's main rail and motorway routes, which helps a team reach the quay quickly once the berth is confirmed.

facilities.h: Where a ship can be gauged in and around Fredericia
p: Fredericia is not a docking port: ships calling here are gauged afloat at their working berth, and dockings are taken elsewhere. At the oil jetties the terminal's safety rules come first. Ultrasonic gauging involves no hot work, but the equipment brought aboard, entry into enclosed spaces and any movement on deck near the manifold are agreed with the terminal and the ship before the team boards. The bulk and breakbulk quays give the freest access, and a ship waiting there for cargo can often be gauged over a day or more. At the container terminal, deck, hatch coaming and lashing-bridge structure and the ballast tanks are reached between crane moves, following the terminal planner's sequence and stopping whenever a crane works over the area.

For a dry docking, ships trading to Fredericia are usually sent to the larger repair yards in Denmark or across the Baltic. Fayard at Lindø, on Odense Fjord, is the nearest yard with big dry docks, and Ørskov Yard at Frederikshavn takes short-sea ships; yards in Poland, Lithuania and Germany are frequent choices too. Gauging the ballast tanks and deck during a Fredericia call a few weeks before the docking lets the superintendent send the yard a steel estimate rather than a guess, and leaves the dock period for the shell, bottom and sea chests that can only be reached with the hull dry.
list: Crude oil export jetty beside the refinery — ballast tank, forepeak and deck gauging on crude tankers during loading, under the terminal's rules.
Product tanker berths — deck plating, cargo lines on deck and segregated ballast tanks on tankers lifting refinery output.
Container terminal — feeder ballast tanks, hatch coamings and deck structure measured between crane moves.
Bulk and breakbulk quays — hold frames and tank tops on bulk carriers, and deck and tween-deck structure on general cargo ships.
Waiting berths in the harbour — longer pre-purchase or condition gauging on ships idle between charters or cargoes.
Fayard dry docks at Lindø, Odense Fjord — shell, bottom and sea chest gauging when a Fredericia trader goes on to dock.

context.h: Port state control, North Sea crude and vetting at Fredericia
p: The Danish Maritime Authority carries out port state control in Fredericia under the Paris MoU, and tankers are among the ship types its inspectors see most often here. Older tankers on short Baltic trades tend to fall into the higher-risk profiles, and a deficiency involving wasted structure, holed air pipes or corroded deck piping can hold a ship until it is measured and repaired or a plan is agreed with class. Oil company vetting runs in parallel: a tanker loading crude or products at the port will normally have been inspected under the OCIMF SIRE programme, and hull condition records, including recent thickness readings, are part of what a vetting inspector or charterer may ask to see.

The energy transition is visible on Fredericia's waterfront too, with plans announced for green fuel production alongside the existing refinery business. EU climate rules now reach shipping directly, through the EU ETS from 2024 and FuelEU Maritime from 2025, and for owners of older tankers and bulk carriers trading to Danish ports they add weight to the choice between another five years of trading, a sale or recycling. Current thickness data is part of making that choice well. Under the EU Ship Recycling Regulation, ships flying an EU flag and other ships of 500 GT and above calling at EU ports must also carry an Inventory of Hazardous Materials, which port state control officers check.

jobs.h: Gauging jobs that come up at Fredericia
jobs.p: Most Fredericia jobs are tied to cargo operations. The superintendent chooses a set of spaces that the crew can empty, ventilate and certify for entry while the ship loads or discharges, and the team works through them in an agreed order so that the critical readings are taken first. Results for each space go to the ship and the office as soon as it is finished, which lets the owner decide before departure whether a repair, a further inspection or a docking is needed. Large renewal-survey programmes are rarely done here; instead, a Fredericia call is used to gauge ahead of a docking, or to follow up a finding by a surveyor, a port state control officer or a vetting inspector. Examples from the port's usual traffic:
list: Ballast tank and forepeak gauging on a crude tanker during loading at the export jetty, ahead of her third renewal survey.
Deck plating and deck cargo pipeline measurement on a product tanker after a vetting observation on corrosion around the manifold.
Hold frame and tank-top readings on a bulk carrier at the bulk quays, following a class recommendation on frame wastage.
Pre-docking gauging of selected ballast tanks on a container feeder, used to fix the steel estimate before she docks at a Baltic yard.
Condition gauging on a general cargo ship waiting for cargo, ordered by a buyer's technical adviser before an offer is confirmed.

logistics: Billund Airport is the closest international airport to Fredericia, and Copenhagen Airport, with frequent intercity trains across Funen to Fredericia station, is the other common route in. The oil terminal and the container and bulk quays are ISPS-controlled, and the oil jetty adds its own safety induction, so the ship's agent sends the team's names and passport details to the terminal ahead of the call. Denmark is in the Schengen area and the team travels from India on Schengen visas, which need applying for well before the ship's expected arrival.
vessels: General cargo and project cargo ships

faqs.q: Can a crude tanker be gauged while she loads at Fredericia?
faqs.a: Partly. Cargo tanks stay closed and inerted while crude is loading, so entry is limited to spaces the ship can certify gas-free: segregated ballast tanks as they are pumped out, the forepeak, void spaces and the deck. Everything is agreed with the master and the terminal beforehand, including the equipment that goes aboard. Cargo tank structure is measured during a docking or a planned period with the tanks cleaned and gas-freed.

faqs.q: Where do ships that call at Fredericia go for dry-docking?
faqs.a: Usually to a larger repair yard elsewhere. The nearest Danish yard with big dry docks is Fayard at Lindø on Odense Fjord, and owners also use yards in Poland, Lithuania and Germany. We can gauge the ship at Fredericia before she leaves for the yard, and send the team on to the yard for the shell and bottom readings once she is dry, using the same TM plan and report layout throughout.

faqs.q: Does the current in the Little Belt affect inspection work?
faqs.a: It affects timing more than the work itself. Berthing and unberthing are planned with the current and the weather, and a ship can be held outside or kept alongside longer than planned when conditions are poor. Our team's boarding time follows the agent's berthing schedule, and if the stay is extended we use the extra hours for spaces that were lower on the priority list rather than leaving them for a later call.

faqs.q: Can product tanker cargo lines be measured on deck at Fredericia?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as the lines are not in use while the readings are taken and the ship's permit system allows the work. Deck cargo lines, vapour return lines, ballast lines crossing the deck and the pipe supports under them are common points of wastage on older product tankers. We record pipe wall readings against nominal thickness with isometric sketches, so the owner can see which spools need renewal.

faqs.q: How quickly can a team reach a ship in Fredericia?
faqs.a: That depends on visas more than distance. Once a Schengen visa is in place, flights from India to Copenhagen or Billund and the onward rail or road journey can be booked as soon as the agent confirms the berth. For owners whose tankers or bulk carriers call regularly, keeping the team's visas current means a job can be accepted at shorter notice when the ship's schedule firms up.
